newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: POSCO agrees in principle to run Hanbo.
newsitem.headline: POSCO agrees in principle to run Hanbo.

text.p: South Korea's Pohang Iron and Steel Co Ltd (POSCO) has agreed in principle to run insolvent Hanbo Steel Co on behalf of its creditors, a POSCO spokesman said on Saturday.
"Yes, we have agreed to the commissioned management of Hanbo," said the spokesman. "But we have not completed negotiations over the management rights."
A Seoul court on Friday froze assets of Hanbo, the country's second largest steelmaker after POSCO, pending a decision on the troubled company's application for court receivership.
POSCO has been selected as a member of a group commissioned to review Hanbo's assets and draw up a plan to normalise the company.
Hanbo Steel, flagship of the Hanbo Group, South Korea's 14th largest conglomerate, defaulted on debt repayments last week. It had accumulated loans totalling five trillion won. ($1 = 863 won)
